items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: The interviewee discusses a movie about Buddy Bolden and compares it to 'Young Man With a Horn', indicating knowledge of the historical figure through media and cultural associations, but no personal interaction is described.

ctx.x: The thing’s not entirely wrong either but when people who know more than you do are telling you things that they know aren’t precisely the way they’re telling you then they’re doing you a favor on one hand but they’re doing you a disservice on another. And it’s up to you to learn, you know, which are the facts and which are the accurate observations and which ones maybe aren’t.

Yeah I remember thinking the movie about Buddy Bolden that came out a couple of years ago was so highly fictionalized, and I assume it was because there’s very little information about him. And to make a whole movie about him, it has to be highly fictionalized I guess.

Well that’s the new version of “Young Man With a Horn” I guess, isn’t it? And nobody pretended, at least at the time, nobody pretended that that was history. People made the associations with Beiderbecke and Berigan because they were obvious examples of somebody with a huge talent that blew it, in the sense of the word.
